# Run Door Contract

  `fgos run` is the primary door for executing new work in the execution core.

  **Two doors, one runUnit — the preferred path for new work.** One task: `fgos run "<prompt>" [--provider <id>]
  [--writes <paths> --worktree <path>]` builds a Unit from the prompt (read-only without `--writes`; `--writes` needs
  a linked worktree; `--provider` is a soft preference, not a pin). Planned work: `fgos workflow start
  <preset>|--units <file>`, one step per Unit. Both bind through `bind()`; the runner commits only the Unit's declared
  `writes` after a passing round, and the worker never runs `git add`/`git commit`. These two doors are the only ones
  that execute work; `fgos dispatch` keeps only the lower-level reads (`decide`, `inspect`, `reconcile`,
  `probe-account`).

  Without `--writes` the Unit runs sandboxed; `--writes` is refused from the main checkout before anything runs. Why
  and when to name `--provider`: `capability-routing-rules`. `--capability` defaults to `execute`. Work already
  written as a Unit file runs as `fgos run --unit <file>`.

  The worker edits files and stops, never running `git add`/`git commit`. After a passing round the runner commits
  only paths inside the Unit's `writes` (subject from the first line of the worker's `summary`); a path the worker
  needs outside that scope goes in `needsWrites`, not on disk.

  herdr is the default transport when present: the worker runs in a watched pane, so a person can follow it live;
  otherwise the call blocks until the Unit settles. Run a long call backgrounded (`run_in_background: true`) and wait
  for the harness's own completion notification — do NOT use `ScheduleWakeup` or polling.

  That wait rule is for a `fgos run` call, which blocks until the Unit settles. `fgos workflow start` returns at once
  with the `workflowRunId` and a `detached` block (`pid`, `logPath`, `statusCommand`) while the run continues in a
  detached process: its output is never the result, so poll `fgos workflow status <workflowRunId>` until the run is
  `completed`, `failed` or parked at a gate. `answer` and `resume` return the same way; pass `--foreground` only when
  the caller must wait in place.
